name: TENG Triboelectric Nanogenerator Mune Film
product_name: Cascades TNG-7 Blade-Surface Triboelectric Nanogenerator Film
description:
A flexible, micron-scale multilayer film that converts sliding mechanical contact — friction between the coated surface and any counterpart material — directly into electrical charge through triboelectric separation. When two dissimilar materials slide against each other, electrons transfer from one surface to the other; the TENG film is engineered to maximize this charge transfer and collect it through a patterned electrode array printed on the film's backing layer, from which it routes to the supercapacitor bank integrated into the tsuka.

Triboelectricity is one of the oldest known electrical phenomena — the amber-and-wool static electricity observed since antiquity — but controlled at nanoscale allows it to be a practical power source. The TNG-7 film achieves this through a nanostructured PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) surface layer over a fluorinated ethylene propylene triboelectric active layer, separated from the patterned aluminum electrode grid by a nylon spacer mesh that allows controlled deformation. When the mune drags across any surface harder than approximately 3 Mohs (concrete, steel, rebar, vehicle panels, rough stone, asphalt), the surface-to-film contact and separation cycle generates charge pulses that the electrode array harvests continuously. A full-pressure drag across ten meters of concrete produces approximately 0.8–1.4 millijoules, depending on drag speed, pressure, and surface texture. The supercapacitor bank charges proportionally.

Critical limitation — humidity sensitivity:
Triboelectric generation requires dry contact. Water films between the TENG surface and the counterpart material act as a conductive bridge that bleeds charge before collection — effectively shorting the generator. At ambient humidity above approximately 70%, TENG film output drops by 60–80%. In active rain or standing water contact, TENG generation approaches zero. In GLMZ's Great Lakes climate — persistent lake-effect humidity, frequent rain, heavy seasonal fog — this is the defining operational constraint of the drag-charging system:

  In dry covered spaces (underground levels, parking structures, industrial floors, building interiors): TENG generation is full-efficiency — the blade charges rapidly on any drag.
  In open-air humid conditions without rain: reduced efficiency, still useful with sustained drag.
  In active rain: TENG generation ceases. The blade must charge exclusively through clash-loading the piezoelectric spine.

This weather dependency is not a manufacturing defect. It is a known characteristic that Torii's Advanced Weapons Division chose to retain because the alternative (a hermetically sealed surface coating) would have eliminated the drag-sparking behavior that made Seo's custom blade tactically distinctive. The film is designed to shed water rapidly — the surface has a contact angle above 150° (superhydrophobic) — but recovery from saturation requires 30–60 seconds of air exposure.
energy_type: Triboelectric — contact electrification between dissimilar surfaces converts kinetic energy of relative motion directly to electrical charge.
historical_development: Triboelectric nanogenerators were first demonstrated in laboratory settings in the early 21st century (Wang et al., 2012) as a potential ambient energy harvesting technology. Early commercial applications focused on wearable electronics harvesting from walking motion. The blade-surface application was Dae-jung Seo's adaptation — integrating Cascades' film into a traditionally constructed laminate blade — and is believed to be the first application of TENG technology to a combat weapon platform. The key engineering insight was that a blade being dragged across a surface creates a high-pressure, high-velocity relative motion event orders of magnitude more energetic than a footstep. The challenge was making a film robust enough to survive the mechanical abuse of repeated hard-surface contact while maintaining triboelectric efficiency.
specifications:
Film thickness: 180–220 microns total stack
Active layer: nanostructured PTFE over FEP triboelectric contact surface
Electrode layer: patterned aluminum grid, 40-micron linewidth
Output voltage: 80–400V AC (peak-to-peak, before rectification)
Output current: 2–15 mA peak during active drag
DC power after rectification and conditioning: 0.5–4 mW continuous during drag
Humidity threshold: >70% ambient = significant output degradation
Operating temperature: -20°C to +120°C
Surface hardness requirement of counterpart: ≥3 Mohs for effective generation
Service life: ~400 heavy drag cycles before electrode delamination begins; field-resurfaceable
tier_availability: Tier 4+ — research and military prototype applications. No civilian commercial version of the blade-surface formulation exists.
developers: TORII SECURITY GROUP — Advanced Weapons Division (integration specification)
enables: Continuous charge accumulation during blade drag against hard surfaces
Pyrophoric spark amplification from underlying ferrocerium substrate during high-pressure drag
Visual and acoustic drag signature (sparks + screech) as combat mode indicator
Weather-dependent tactical charging: reliable indoors, degraded in rain
limitations: Humidity and rain suppress output to near zero — this is the blade's primary tactical weakness
Film degrades through cumulative heavy-contact cycles — periodic resurfacing required
High output voltage requires rectification and conditioning before supercapacitor storage
Zero output in standing water or sustained rain — operator must rely on clash-charging (piezo spine) in wet conditions

cost.installation_labor: Self-applicable with care — adhesion tools and surface prep required. Professional application recommended: Φ 300–600 additional.
cost.availability: Cascades Energy Systems distributes to military and licensed research contractors only. Gray market access through defense contractor intermediaries. 2–4 week lead time typical.
cost.notes: ~400 heavy drag cycles before electrode delamination begins. Field-resurfaceable without removing the blade from service.
